title: None of the four upper confidence bounds is the one the data support
published: with 95% confidence intervals extending from -0.325 to [[-0.025]] for the indirect effect and -0.575 to [[0.000]] for the direct effect. [...] The 95% confidence intervals are much wider, at [-0.325, [[0.200]]] for the indirect effect and [-0.625, [[0.175]]] for the direct effect
corrected: with 95% confidence intervals extending from -0.325 to [[-0.050]] for the indirect effect and -0.575 to [[-0.025]] for the direct effect. [...] The 95% confidence intervals are much wider, at [-0.325, [[0.175]]] for the indirect effect and [-0.625, [[0.200 or higher]]] for the direct effect
note: The bounds are read off the p-value surfaces saved in the corrigendum's own archive (doi:10.7910/DVN/H47CC6, fig2.rdata), the original panel for the first pair of intervals and the corrected panel for the second. The function that located them returned the first grid point after each edge of the confidence region, which is the first point inside at the lower edge and the first point outside at the upper edge, so three of the four upper bounds sit one step of 0.025 too high. The fourth, the corrected direct bound, lies at the top of the grid searched: the region runs to 0.2, where the function returns no bound at all, so the printed 0.175 has no origin in the code, and the data place the bound no lower than 0.2. The lower bounds are correct. Corrected, the original intervals still exclude zero and the corrected ones still include it, which is the corrigendum's conclusion.
